findings:

🔵 [test-t4-t13-helpers] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The T4 and T13 tests reference a local `readEventsNoCancel` defined at the bottom of the file; vitest hoists hoisted? No — these are top-level `async function` declarations so they resolve before the `describe` blocks run. It is correct, just non-obvious; not blocking.
🟠 [store-fetch-inbox-ids-after-handle-escape] MUST-FIX `fetchInboxIdsAfter` interpolates `to_handle` directly into a SQL LIKE clause (`to_handle NOT LIKE '@mailbox:%'`), and the `directClause` builder also inlines the `to_handle` value into a literal pattern. With a pollerInstance the same handle is bound twice via positional placeholders, which is safe for SQL injection but the LIKE constant `'@mailbox:%'` and the team/from_handle binding are still handled correctly. The real concern: the route passes `pollerInstance` to `fetchInboxIdsAfter` for the poller-side tail count, but `fetchInboxIdsAfter` ignores it for the filter on `meta_json->>'$.sender_instance'` when pollerInstance is undefined (fine), yet the route always passes pollerInstance for tail counts — verify the count excludes self-sent rows for parity with the deliverable gate. Re-check: deliverable gate uses `sender_instance != pollerInstance`; the new helper does the same. OK, but the unfiltered (no pollerInstance) branch lacks the guard — must be unreachable from the route. Confirm: route always passes pollerInstance. If true, this is fine; otherwise `pending_after` overcounts. Smallest fix: assert/reject pollerInstance === undefined at the top of the route's tail-count block.
🔵 [scan-cap-off-by-one] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `scanBacklog` sets `capped = true` when `pending + exempt >= BACKLOG_SCAN_CAP`, breaking BEFORE incrementing the 10 001st row — so `newest` is the 10 000th. The T16 test asserts exactly that. Good. No defect.
🔵 [by-sender-team-fold] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `foldBySender` sorts by descending count then name; `@team` rows are bucketed under `TEAM_BROADCAST_HANDLE` in scanBacklog. T19 verifies behavior. No defect.
